changeBrief: PR #16 adds semantic release automation backed by a repository-scoped GitHub App, enforces release workflow policy through repository validation, adds continuous OpenSSF Scorecard analysis, and introduces a two-job SPDX publication path that generates an SBOM under read-only permissions and publishes an immutable draft release only after artifact validation and checksum verification.

changeScope.evidence: 29 changed files and 2,787 insertions; executable changes span three workflows, release configuration, two SPDX scripts, the repository validator, and two test modules, with the remaining volume in durable review and RPI records.

pathCriticality.evidence: The change crosses long-lived App credential handling, short-lived repository-write tokens, tag creation, draft and immutable release mutation, cross-job artifact transfer, shell/API boundaries, and SBOM parsing.

history.evidence: Thirteen commits show repeated CCR and supply-chain redesign around trigger behavior, authentication, governance, release immutability, and SBOM publication.

testPresence.evidence: The branch includes exact workflow/config validators, negative mutation tests, SPDX preparation/validation tests, a real checksummed Syft generation run, and green hosted CI.

coverage.evidence: No end-to-end version tag, draft release, asset upload, checksum verification, or immutable publication has executed on GitHub because the workflow is not yet on main.

rollback.evidence: Tracked changes are revertible before release, but an immutable published release is intentionally hard to reverse; failed runs can leave a tag and draft release requiring operational recovery.

depthRationale: The user selected comprehensive depth because this is a security-sensitive release path with durable external state, cross-job trust boundaries, and no end-to-end production execution.
outOfScope: accessibility: no user interface or interactive end-user surface changed
